costs-and-registration.title: Costs & Registration FIRST Tech Challenge | IFR Foundation
costs-and-registration.description: All information you need to run FIRST Tech Challenge Team in Indonesia. By Indonesia FIRST Robotik.
costs-and-registration.heading: Costs & Registration
costs-and-registration.subheading: All information you need about the costs to run a team and registration cost.
costs-and-registration.about-registering-desc-1: Creating a new team in FTC Dashboard is free, however, registering your team in a season will costs you some money.
costs-and-registration.about-registering-list-1: Official FIRST Tech Challenge team number
costs-and-registration.about-registering-list-2: Ability to register and compete in official remote or in-person FIRST Tech Challenge events (varies by region)
costs-and-registration.about-registering-list-3: Access to the FIRST storefront for discounted control system components and robot kit of parts
costs-and-registration.about-registering-list-4: Access to resources for team management and career readiness
costs-and-registration.about-registering-list-5: Ability to compete for team awards and FIRST Tech Challenge Dean’s List Award
costs-and-registration.about-registering-list-6: Team member and alumni access to career discovery opportunities, networking, and the
costs-and-registration.season-registration-desc: All costs for individual team members are assumed by the team as a group. Registered teams also receive complimentary access to FIRST fundraising tools and resources to help teams create their own opportunities. Needs-based grants and sponsorships for teams may also be available locally, regionally, and nationally by many corporations.
costs-and-registration.season-registration-info: Season team registration for North American teams is $295. International team registration varies by location. Exact costs will be known after registered to FIRST.
costs-and-registration.regional-events-fees-desc: After you’ve registered your team on FIRST website, you can then register your team on IFR to be able to join in Indonesia FTC Regional Competition! Good luck team!
costs-and-registration.additional-costs-list-1: A reusable robot kit of parts required for game play with purchase options starting at about $1,000. Season team registration fee does not include shipping and handling, robot control system hardware, or robot kits.
costs-and-registration.additional-costs-list-2: Additional fees for registration to local and/or remote FIRST Tech Challenge events. These fees are set and collected by the local Program Delivery Partner. Season team registration does not guarantee events are available in your area.
costs-and-registration.rev-kit-parts-link-text: To purchase your kit of parts, please visit FIRST team Dashboard: https://login2.firstinspires.org/Account/Login.
costs-and-registration.rev-kit-parts-desc: You will then be able to access the Pitsco Storefront to purchase your robotics kit. There are a couple choices you’ll be able to make to select the kit that will work best for your team.

info-for-volunteers.title: Volunteer | IFR Foundation
info-for-volunteers.description: Information for FIRST Tech Challenge information
info-for-volunteers.hero-subtitle: Volunteering at Indonesia FIRST Robotik Foundation
info-for-volunteers.hero-title: Together we empower the next generation of science and technology leaders.
info-for-volunteers.hero-title-part4: next generation of science and technology leaders.
info-for-volunteers.first-desc: FIRST is the world's leading education association for the study of science, technology, engineering and mathematics among children and teenagers. FIRST encourages children and youth to become science leaders through robotics programs based on hands-on learning, exposing students to engineering and programming in an engaging, inclusive and creative learning environment, where they work collaboratively to solve an annual robotics challenge.
info-for-volunteers.journey-title: Your journey to influence the future starts here
info-for-volunteers.journey-desc: When you volunteer with FIRST, you foster valuable skills among children and youth. You are building the next generation of science and technology leaders. You inspire them to use their skills to make a positive impact on their communities and the world. You are brightening the future for millions of young people around the world.
info-for-volunteers.volunteer-opportunity: Volunteering with FIRST is an amazing opportunity for you to be full of energy and have fun. If you are looking for an exciting and inspiring environment to make a difference, there is a place for you as a volunteer at FIRST ! There are various positions ranging from award judging, guidance, technical help and more.

ftc-page.title: FIRST Tech Challenge Indonesia | IFR Foundation
ftc-page.description: FIRST Tech Challenge is a Robotics program by FIRST for middle school and high school students. Students are challenged to design, build, program, and operate robots to compete in a head-to-head challenge in an alliance format. Here in Indonesia FIRST Robotics, we are bringing FIRST Tech Challenge to Indonesia!

ftc-start-a-team.title: Start an FTC Team | IFR Foundation
ftc-start-a-team.description: Step by step guide with resources to start your own FIRST Tech Challenge team in Indonesia.
ftc-start-a-team.heading: Start A New Team
ftc-start-a-team.subheading: Our step by step guide on how to start your team.
ftc-start-a-team.info-box-desc: You are able to start your own FTC team in your community with private funds or sponsor funds.
ftc-start-a-team.info-box-note: FIRST does not match youth to existing teams due to FIRST privacy policy. Teams form in local communities and recruit as needed. We encourage those looking for a team to contact local schools, libraries, or youth organizations that may have a team in place or an interest in starting one. An online search may also be helpful, as some teams share contact information through websites and social media pages.
ftc-start-a-team.step1-title: Familiarise Yourself With FIRST Tech Challenge
ftc-start-a-team.step1-desc: FIRST Tech Challenge is much more than a robotics competition. This is a program that teaches students the meaning and value of investment and challenging work, entrepreneurship and creativity while having pure enjoyment based on challenge and joint effort. Throughout the program, the students will recognize and internalize the importance of teamwork, sharing knowledge and ideas and the importance of mutual respect, courtesy to competitors and involvement in the community.
ftc-start-a-team.step2-desc: As part of the program, 8th to 12th grade students face a technological challenge to build a robot that competes in a challenging competition with a central theme that is updated every year. With the exception of the technological knowledge that includes programming, construction, mechanics, electricity, electronics and more, the process of building the robot and the format of the competition also integrate the development of skills and abilities that include - strategic thinking, creativity, resource management, problem solving, project management, teamwork and documentation of engineering processes Notebook.
ftc-start-a-team.step3-desc: To establish a team, several important things are required: Commitment of the school principal to the program.
ftc-start-a-team.step3-list2: The team consists of a leading teacher and another 1-2 adults in mentor/coach roles.
ftc-start-a-team.step3-list3: A safe work workshop that includes basic tools and equipment in the first stage to plan, design, build, program, and test the robot you will build.
ftc-start-a-team.step4-desc: Visit www.firstinspires.org/register to create your FIRST ® account, set up your new team profile, and purchase your season registration and necessary materials.
ftc-start-a-team.step4-link2: Step by Step Guide Team Registration Walkthrough (Youtube)
ftc-start-a-team.step5-desc: Read and understand the season game manual, it is really important for all team members to understand the game and season.
ftc-start-a-team.step5-note: Link above is up to date to current season.
ftc-start-a-team.step6-desc: Review the season materials and design, construct, and program your robot to compete in the season game, and document your work in an engineering portfolio
ftc-start-a-team.step7-desc: Team can join in local area event, step up to regional event, and all the way to the FTC World Championship. Good luck team!

about-first.title: About FIRST | IFR Foundation
about-first.description: Information About FIRST, For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology.
about-first.hero-subtitle: The World's Leading Youth-Serving Nonprofit Advancing STEAM Education
about-first.more-than-robots-desc:
Founded in 1989 by inventor Dean Kamen, FIRST® (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) is a global nonprofit (501(c)(3)) organization that prepares young people for the future through a suite of inclusive in interest and participation in science and technology. Based in Manchester, innovative programs that motivate young people to pursue education and career opportunities in science, technology, engineering, and math, while building self-confidence, knowledge, and life skills.

These programs, based on hands-on learning, expose students to engineering and programming in a fascinating, inclusive and creative learning environment, where they work collaboratively to solve an annual robotics challenge, combining excitement, creativity and cultivating valuable skills in the real world, including self-confidence, communication, teamwork, Decision making, experience in planning and managing resources, leadership skills and more.
about-first.vision-desc: To transform our culture by creating a world where science and technology are celebrated and where young people dream of becoming science and technology leaders.
about-first.mission-desc: The mission of FIRST is to inspire young people to be science and technology leaders, by engaging them in exciting mentor-based programs that build science, engineering and technology skills, that inspire innovation, and that foster well-rounded life capabilities including self-confidence, communication, and leadership.
about-first.gracious-desc: Gracious Professionalism, introduced by Dr. Woodie Flowers and integral to FIRST's ethos, advocates for high-quality work, values others, and respects individuals and the community. It encourages spirited competition with mutual benefit, highlighting respectful and empathetic interactions while avoiding negativity.
about-first.coopertition-desc: Coopertition cultivates innovation by advocating unwavering kindness and respect amid fierce competition. In FIRST, Coopertition entails teams assisting and collaborating with one another, embracing a culture of learning from teammates, teaching others, working with mentors, and both managing and being managed. It encapsulates the essence of competing while actively supporting and empowering others whenever opportunities arise.

home-page.hero-subtitle: A Home to the Indonesian youth FIRST® robotics.
home-page.impacts-subheading: and helping them realize their power to build a better future
home-page.impacts-description: As we work as a community to prepare young people for a STEM future, FIRST aims to ensure its programs are having a lasting, positive impact on participants across all demographic groups. Our rigorous multi-year longitudinal study, conducted by Brandeis University Center for Youth and Communities, provides strong evidence that participation in FIRST does just that. Even with just one year of FIRST participation, study participants are 2-3xs more likely to have gains in STEM outcomes than a comparison group of peers not participating in FIRST.
